description: A family leaving for several weeks needs to brief a house sitter on alarms, deliveries, watering routines, utility shutoffs, known quirks, and what counts as an emergency versus a wait-until-return issue.

user_profile.persona: 40-year-old parent coordinating departure logistics for a long trip
user_profile.context: The house sitter is trustworthy but unfamiliar with the home's systems and recurring quirks
user_profile.communication_style: Preventive and specific, wants a handoff note that reduces avoidable calls

fact_sheet.fact: The security system disarm code is 1-2-5-8.
To arm the system when leaving, press the 'Away' button and enter the code 1-2-5-8; you will have 60 seconds to exit.
The monitoring company, Sentinel Secure Systems, will call from 555-0188 if the alarm is triggered.
If you accidentally trigger the alarm, the safe word to give the monitoring company is 'Blue Jay'.
The main security system keypad is located on the wall to the left of the door leading from the garage into the kitchen.
The key for mailbox #7B is in the small ceramic bowl on the entryway console table.
Our large package delivery box, a ParcelDrop Box, is located by the garage door and the access code is 9-8-7-6.
We are expecting a package from 'CraftyKits' containing yarn, scheduled to arrive around July 15th.
The 'Crestwood Chronicle' newspaper delivery has been paused and will resume on August 5th; please discard any papers delivered by mistake.
The cat, Whiskers, eats 1/2 cup of 'Purrfect Morsels' dry food at 8 AM and 6 PM daily.
The cat's food is stored in a large blue bin labeled 'Whiskers' on the top left shelf of the kitchen pantry.
The litter box, located in the laundry room, should be scooped daily.
Water the fiddle-leaf fig in the living room with 2 cups of water every Saturday morning.
The three tomato plants in pots on the back patio need to be watered every other day, preferably before 10 AM.
In case of a pet emergency, contact Dr. Evans at Crestwood Animal Hospital at 555-0123.
The main water shutoff valve is in the basement on the back wall, behind the furnace, and has a red handle.
The main electrical circuit breaker panel is in the garage, on the wall to the left of the interior door to the house.
The gas shutoff wrench is hanging on a hook next to the gas meter on the exterior west wall of the house.
The Wi-Fi network name is 'MillerHomeNet' and the password is 'Trip2Europe!'.
The deadbolt on the back patio door sticks; you must pull the door firmly toward you while turning the key to lock it.
The garbage disposal switch is not on the wall; it is a black push-button located under the sink cabinet, on the right side.
If the toilet in the upstairs guest bathroom continues to run after flushing, jiggle the silver flush handle to make it stop.
The kitchen outlets are on breaker #12, which can trip if you run the microwave and the toaster oven at the same time.
The 'EcoHome' smart thermostat is programmed to lower the AC to 68°F at 10 PM; please do not override this schedule.
An emergency is defined as an unstoppable water leak, any sign of fire, or a security breach.
A non-emergency issue, such as a burnt-out lightbulb or slow internet, can wait until we return.
Our next-door neighbor, Sarah Jenkins, has a spare key. Her number is 555-0199 and she lives at 458 Maple Creek Drive.
For a major plumbing emergency like a burst pipe, call Reliable Rooter Plumbing at 555-0150.
The fire extinguisher is located under the kitchen sink, behind the cleaning supplies.
Trash day is Tuesday morning. Please put the black bin (garbage) and blue bin (recycling) on the curb Monday night.

user_needs.description: How do I disarm the security system when I arrive and where is the keypad located?
What is the procedure for arming the system when I leave the house?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After learning how to disarm the system, the user will naturally want to know the opposite procedure for arming it.

user_needs.description: What should I do if I accidentally trigger the alarm, and what is the safe word?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Discussing the alarm system's operation naturally leads to considering what to do if something goes wrong.

user_needs.description: If the alarm goes off and Sentinel Secure calls, what number will they call from and what safe word do I need to give?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning what to do if they trigger the alarm, the most direct follow-up is how to handle the monitoring company's call if the alarm sounds.

user_needs.description: What are the cat's daily feeding and litter instructions?
What is the watering schedule for the indoor and outdoor plants?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After covering pet care, the other main daily/weekly routine is typically plant care.

user_needs.description: Who is the emergency contact for the cat?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning the standard pet care routine, a responsible sitter would want to know the procedure for a pet-related emergency.

user_needs.description: How do I handle mail, packages, and the weekly trash/recycling pickup?
Are there any operational quirks I should know about, like with the back door lock, garbage disposal, or a specific toilet?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After covering external tasks like mail and trash, the user's focus naturally shifts to how things work inside the house, especially non-obvious issues.

user_needs.description: What defines a major emergency and where is the main water shutoff valve?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Discussing minor operational quirks is a natural springboard to considering major problems and emergency procedures.

user_needs.description: For a major plumbing emergency, who do I call, and where is the fire extinguisher?
user_needs.prediction_reason: This is a direct follow-up to the definition of an emergency, seeking specific contacts and locations for the scenarios mentioned.
